text: Given a /mcp request missing the X-Telivy-Api-Key header, When any tool is invoked, Then the service returns HTTP 401 naming the missing header, and the mocked Telivy endpoint is never called.
evidence: pytest node above passed. Also verified live: `curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/mcp -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}'` (no credential header) against the running server returned `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` with body `{"error":"Missing credentials","message":"This server requires the X-Telivy-Api-Key header","required_headers":["X-Telivy-Api-Key"],"optional_headers":[]}` -- the middleware 401s before the MCP method dispatcher runs, so no tool (and no outbound Telivy call) is ever reached.

text: Given two concurrent requests carrying two different tenants' API keys, When each calls telivy_list_external_scans at the same time, Then each receives only its own tenant's data, with no cross-contamination from shared state.
evidence: Both pytest nodes above passed. The middleware test interleaves two asyncio tasks carrying different X-Telivy-Api-Key values through GatewayTokenMiddleware and asserts each task's handler sees only its own key via the contextvar; the tools test confirms get_client_from_context() builds a fresh TelivyClient scoped to whatever key is in context at call time, with no module-level cache.
notes: exception/boundary, multi-tenant isolation, hits the request-handling layer (not just UI/gating)

text: Given Telivy returns 404 / 429 / a 5xx-or-timeout for an upstream call, When the tool maps the response, Then it returns {"error":{"code":"not_found"|"rate_limited"|"upstream_error", "retryable": ...}} with the correct retryable value and no raw upstream body or credential in the message.
evidence: All pytest nodes above passed (status-to-code/retryable mapping parametrized over 400/401/403/404/422/429/500/503; a 404 response with extra fields like internal_trace_id and another tenant's domain name is confirmed absent from the resulting envelope; a transient 429 is retried and succeeds; a persistent 429 and a simulated httpx.ConnectError both raise the correctly-classified TelivyError).
notes: exception/boundary, three sub-cases (404/429/5xx) covered by a parametrized test module plus dedicated retry/network-error tests

text: Given a list tool is called with no limit or a limit above the hard cap, When the response is built, Then the effective page size is clamped (default <=50, hard cap <=200); if the result would exceed the 20,000-character budget, Then the tool truncates and sets has_more=true instead of erroring or silently dropping data.
evidence: All pytest nodes above passed: clamp_limit is parametrized over None/1/50/200/201/100000 -> 50/1/50/200/200/200; a tool call with limit=5000 is confirmed to send limit=200 upstream (never Telivy's own 100 default, never the caller's 5000); dump_json_capped on a 1000-item payload with a 2000-char budget truncates to under the budget with truncated=true, has_more=true, and the true original_count preserved, while a small payload passes through byte-for-byte.
